Thanks Anita — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-cut MAP and sequencing manifest (Redwood_Seamline_MAP_v1.xlsx) that maps pilot evaluation milestones to legal/procurement milestones. High-level summary here:

- Week 0–1: Pilot acceptance (technical) — evidence: eval report, basic SOC checklist. No PII exchange.
- Week 2: Legal review window for MSA (commercial terms) — Redwood provides annotated MSA for Novamed counsel.
- Week 3: DPA parallel review — we can run DPA redlines in parallel with MSA, but we request an agreed temp data handling statement (Annex A) before production access.
- Week 4: Order form finalization (pricing, seat counts, start date) — PO routing can start; sign-off contingent on MSA & DPA alignment or an explicit conditional acceptance clause.
- Week 5–6: Signatures & enablement — target DocuSign routing; early provisioning for staging once redlines are agreed.

Key callouts:
- The DPA can be executed on a parallel track; in practice we accept a conditional order form that references the DPA execution (i.e., order becomes effective subject to DPA signature within X days).
- If Novamed requires DPA first (legal policy), we can accommodate but it commonly adds ~1 week.
- To hit a ~6-week close, we need Novamed counsel to confirm a 5-business-day review SLA per round for redlines.

I've flagged two high-risk clauses for discussion in the annotated MSA: indemnity scope and data residency annex ordering. Laura and Neha will coordinate legal/ops input.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min call tomorrow 11am PT to walk the MAP.
2) Novamed confirms counsel contact and review SLA.
3) Redwood uploads annotated MSA & DPA (MSA_DPA_annotated_v3.pdf attached).

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Seamline commitment map & acceptance manifest (MSA/DPA/order form sequencing)

Hi all — I reviewed the annotated MSA & DPA (v3) and pulled two items Novamed counsel will likely drive on that will affect sequencing:

1) Liability cap carveouts — Novamed counsel may request a recasting of SLA/availability remedies into a defined credit schedule rather than indemnity. That typically requires procurement sign-off and may delay commercial sign-off by 3–5 business days.

2) Data processing sub-processor list & audit rights — if Novamed requires an audit clause in the DPA (rather than targeted rights), we will need to scope which environments are auditable; that may require an addendum and push the DPA sign-off timeline.

Options to keep to the 6-week runway:
- Option A (preferred): Execute MSA with conditional DPA language (order form becomes effective subject to DPA signature within 10 business days). This keeps procurement moving and allows security team to complete evidence exchange.
- Option B: Parallel sign-off with a small carve to hold funds or escrow until DPA is final (procurement dependent).

I recommend we lock Week 2–3 for rapid redline exchange and ask Novamed counsel to confirm their review SLA. If James is able to do a quick triage call with me tomorrow, I can accelerate the annotated callouts to a short list for negotiation.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
